info.title: Expenditure API
info.description: Personal API keys authorize personal expense automation and self-paid Circle expense creation. Circle management, reads and split edits require a normal PocketBase users session in the Authorization header. Ownership, membership, currency precision, splits, and settlements are validated on the server. Requests and stored records use amount (integer currency minor units) and payment_method. Field aliases are not accepted. Income uses positive amounts and kind=income; spending reports and budgets include expenses only. Recurring income and expenses run on the PocketBase server every minute, with custom intervals and monthly dates, catching up after downtime. Schedule edits affect future copies; stopping or deleting the original preserves generated entries.

post.description: Requires expenses:write. New expenses use preferences.default_api_circle: empty saves personally; a Circle ID saves directly in that Circle with merchant mapped internally to title. The request accepts merchant, never title; other fields retain their names. Omitted currency and category use the destination defaults. Supplied categories must be active in that destination, and supplied personal currencies must be enabled. No personal expense copy is created for Circle imports. Circle imports are self-paid and initially 100% self-allocated. Responses return the stored Expense (merchant) or CircleExpense (title, circle), plus destination, replay and idempotency_expires_at. The preference applies across all of the user's keys and affects creation only; existing retries retain their original destination, including after preference changes. Explicit Circle URLs ignore the preference. Unavailable defaults return 404 without falling back to personal. Idempotency-Key is optional and shared across both expense creation endpoints, scoped to the user across API keys. The fixed 24-hour window starts at the original server-created timestamp and survives transaction edits or deletion. Identical accepted data replays the current transaction; changed data or a different explicitly targeted Circle conflicts. Omitted defaults resolve against the immutable original request on replay. Retries never extend the window. After expiry the key can create a new expense. A deleted transaction returns 410 during the window; an unavailable Circle or inactive membership returns 404. Failed writes do not consume a key. New Circle entries require Add permission, checked inside the write transaction. Existing idempotent retries can replay after Add permission is revoked.

patch.summary: Author, owner or Admin: edit a recorded repayment
patch.description: Updates a recorded external repayment without transferring money. Requires its current version. The original author, Circle owner or an Admin may edit. Financial changes by an ordinary member require that author to remain a participant in the replacement; metadata-only edits retain author access. Financial changes are validated against current balances with the original repayment reversed, so they cannot overpay or mix currencies. Former members balances cannot change. The ID, original creator and creation timestamp are retained. Omitted notes and occurred_at retain their previous values. Notes/date-only edits remain allowed after later ledger changes. Balances and repayment suggestions are recalculated from the saved ledger.

get.summary: Get monthly spending and income totals
get.description: Aggregates all matching personal expenses and, when preferences.include_circle_in_budgets is enabled (the default), the requesting user's positive allocated shares of Circle expenses, regardless of who paid. Uses the expense instant and supplied account-timezone month boundaries, including historical shares for inactive memberships. Moved personal receipts are excluded to prevent double counting. Circle categories match personal categories by exact name, then by a unique case/whitespace-insensitive name; unmatched or ambiguous names count as the personal Other category or a report-only Other bucket. Split edits update consumption without creating personal transactions or changing Circle balances. Circle income and repayments do not consume budgets. Native personal collection lists remain personal-only. The Transactions page and its exports can use the preference-aware combined transaction feed.

post.summary: Move an owned personal expense to a Circle
post.description: Active members with Add permission may transfer their own expense. Income cannot be moved. Atomically excludes the original from the personal ledger and creates a Circle expense with the same ID, amount, currency, occurrence, created/updated timestamps, notes, payment method and provenance. Payer and author are the moving membership ID. Initial percentage split is 10000 basis points to that member, adding no debt. Recurrence and its saved timezone, anchor, next cursor and pause state transfer intact; existing generated personal entries stay in place. Retries to the same Circle return the existing entry without duplicating or overwriting it. A retained owner-protected receipt preserves API idempotency for the original 24-hour window, even if the Circle entry is later deleted. Transfers do not return to the personal ledger when a Circle is deleted. New Circle entries require Add permission, checked inside the write transaction. Existing idempotent retries can replay after Add permission is revoked.

Identical accepted data replays the current transaction; changed data or a different explicitly targeted Circle conflicts. Omitted defaults resolve against the immutable original request on replay. Retries never extend the window. After expiry the key can create a new expense. A deleted transaction returns 410 during the window; an unavailable Circle or inactive membership returns 404. Failed writes do not consume a key. New Circle entries require Add permission, checked inside the write transaction. Existing idempotent retries can replay after Add permission is revoked.

get.summary: List personal transactions with optional allocated Circle entries
get.description: Session-only feed controlled by the requesting account show_circle_transactions preference. Positive own Circle expense and income shares are included when enabled, regardless of payer, including retained inactive membership history. Zero/unallocated entries, repayments and moved personal receipts are excluded. Filtering, counts and descending occurred_at/created/collectionName/id ordering apply to the complete combined dataset before pagination. Native record fields remain unchanged: Circle amount is the full original amount; allocated_amount is the account share; budget_category maps the Circle category to the personal account. No personal record copies or financial mutations are made. Personal automation read scopes do not grant access.

post.summary: Move a Circle expense or income to your personal ledger
post.description: Normal users session only. Requires active Circle membership and independent move_scope permission: none denies moves, payer requires paid_by to equal the actor’s membership ID, and all allows any entry. Edit permission neither grants nor restricts moves. Owners and Admins have all Move access. The new personal entry always belongs to the authenticated actor, even when someone else paid. Atomically removes the Circle entry and creates a fresh personal entry with the full positive amount and original kind, currency (even when disabled personally), occurrence, created/updated timestamps, payment method, notes and provenance. A supplied category must be an active personal category ID owned by the user. Omission matches active personal categories by exact name, then a unique case/whitespace-insensitive name, then Other, then the first active category. Removes all Circle allocations and recalculates balances while preserving former-member balances and recorded repayments. Recurrence timezone, calendar controls, anchor, cursor and pause error move intact; earlier generated entries stay in the Circle. No move receipt or original split/receipt snapshot is retained. After a successful move, repeated requests return 404 because the Circle source no longer exists. If a response is lost, refresh both ledgers to confirm the result. Earlier personal-to-Circle receipts remain immutable. Circle API idempotency receipts keep their original destination and return 410 after this move rather than recreating the entry.

patch.summary: Owner or Admin: set permissions for an active member
patch.description: Set Admin access and independent Add, Edit, Delete and Move to personal permissions for expenses and income. Own entries are identified by created_by, not paid_by. The current owner or an Admin may change active members, including granting and revoking Admin access. The owner cannot be restricted. Admin grants full access to transactions, settings, categories, invitations, other member management and repayments. Removing the owner, transferring ownership and deleting the Circle are prohibited for Admins. Version checks prevent overwriting concurrent permission changes. Permissions are enforced inside every transaction. Existing and new members default to Admin disabled, Add allowed, Edit own and Delete own. Rejoining retains saved permissions. Permission changes do not alter ledger records, balances or repayment records. Admins have the same repayment management permissions as the owner, while ordinary members retain their existing repayment permissions. Revoked Add access pauses future recurring generation with a visible error; restore access and edit the schedule to resume. API idempotency replays and confirmed personal-to-Circle move retries still replay existing entries after Add is revoked. Move scope is independent of Edit: none denies moves, payer requires paid_by to match the actor’s membership, and all allows any entry to move to the actor’s personal ledger. New members default to payer; upgrades use none when stored Edit was none, otherwise payer. Owners and Admins have all Move access.

recurrence.description: Empty disables recurrence for expenses or income. Only the original entry holds a schedule; generated copies have empty recurrence, zero interval/day/month and empty weekdays. Enabling, changing or resuming starts strictly after both the entry instant and now; active schedules catch up after downtime. Occurrences retain the entry wall-clock time in the saved timezone. Monthly and yearly dates clamp to shorter months without losing the requested day.

recurrence_interval.description: Repeat every N days, weeks, months or years. Active schedules store 1 to 365; omitted or zero selects 1. Disabled schedules and generated entries store 0.

recurrence_day.description: Monthly or yearly schedules: 0 keeps the original calendar day, -1 selects the last day of the scheduled month, and 1 to 31 selects that day, clamped in shorter months. Explicit dates may recur later in the original month or year. Other frequencies require 0.

recurrence_timezone.description: Account timezone captured when the schedule starts.

recurrence_anchor.description: Original local calendar date/time; month ends clamp without losing this day.

recurrence_next.description: Next occurrence as an ISO instant, or empty when disabled.

recurrence_error.description: Non-empty means generation is paused. Resolve the issue and save the schedule to retry.

moved_to.description: Transferred Circle expense ID. Non-empty only on an API-key idempotency replay receipt; transferred rows are excluded from personal lists, reports and exports.

moved_circle.description: Destination Circle ID on a transfer receipt.

recurrence_weekdays.description: Weekly only: ISO weekdays (Monday=1, Sunday=7), stored in ascending order. Empty selects the original entry weekday. Weeks start Monday; every-N-week schedules remain anchored to the original entry week. Selected days later in the original week can recur. Other frequencies require an empty array.

recurrence_month.description: Yearly only: month 1 to 12, or 0 to use the original entry month. The year interval stays anchored to the entry year. Other frequencies require 0.

default_tab.description: Page opened after sign-in. API keys are managed under Settings → API; upgrades replace the former API keys landing-page choice with Settings.

time_format.description: Persisted display preference for all app times and local export columns. New and upgraded accounts default to 24h. API and UTC timestamps retain ISO notation; stored instants and recurrence schedules do not change.

include_circle_in_budgets.description: Includes positive allocated Circle expense shares in personal monthly budgets and spending summaries. Enabled by default for new and upgraded accounts. Independent of show_circle_transactions; disabling excludes Circle shares from current and previous totals, categories, activity, counts and conversion warnings without changing the Circle ledger.

show_circle_transactions.description: Shows personal transactions and positive own Circle expense/income allocations together in dashboard recent transactions, the Transactions page and its exports. Off by default for new and upgraded accounts. Does not change monthly budgets or spending summaries.

default_api_circle.description: Default destination for new expenses submitted to POST /api/expenses/transactions across all user API keys. Empty means personal workspace; otherwise an active Circle ID. Retained after Circle deletion or membership loss so new API writes fail clearly until changed. Explicit Circle URLs and existing idempotency retries retain their destinations.

default_entry_currency.description: Preferred currency for new personal expense and income forms. Empty follows the main currency; a selected currency must be enabled. Disabling that currency resets this preference to empty. Does not change existing transactions, budgets, recurring generation, Circle entries or API import defaults.

default_expense_category.description: Optional single relation ID of an active personal category owned by this user, used to prefill new personal expense forms. Empty selects Other, then the first active category. Renames preserve the selection; archiving clears matching defaults atomically. Existing transactions, Circle entries and API import defaults are unchanged.

default_income_category.description: Optional single relation ID of an active personal category owned by this user, used to prefill new personal income forms. Empty selects Other, then the first active category. Renames preserve the selection; archiving clears matching defaults atomically. Existing transactions, Circle entries and API import defaults are unchanged.

Preferences.description: Persisted per-account preferences, editable through the owner-protected PocketBase preferences collection.

currency.description: A supported uppercase currency code enabled in the user account. Defaults to the user main currency only when omitted; null, empty strings and non-string values are rejected.

category.description: Personal category ID. Website/session writes require an active category owned by the user; an unchanged archived category remains valid on edits.

occurred_at.description: Defaults to server time; include Z or a timezone offset when supplied.

notes.description: Optional text, preserved as supplied, up to 2000 characters. Defaults to an empty string.

amount.description: Positive integer currency minor units, stored unchanged as amount in PocketBase. SGD 6.50 = 650, JPY 1000 = 1000, KWD 1.234 = 1234.

payment_method.description: Optional free-text payment label, such as Cash or Visa, stored unchanged as payment_method. Defaults to an empty string.

kind.description: Positive amount with an explicit direction. For Circle income, paid_by is the recipient who owes each member their allocated share.

recurrence.description: Empty disables recurrence for expenses or income. Only the original entry holds a schedule; generated copies have empty recurrence, zero interval/day/month and empty weekdays. Enabling, changing or resuming starts strictly after both the entry instant and now; active schedules catch up after downtime. Occurrences retain the entry wall-clock time in the saved timezone. Monthly and yearly dates clamp to shorter months without losing the requested day.

recurrence_interval.description: Repeat every N days, weeks, months or years. Active schedules store 1 to 365; omitted or zero selects 1. Disabled schedules and generated entries store 0.

recurrence_day.description: Monthly or yearly schedules: 0 keeps the original calendar day, -1 selects the last day of the scheduled month, and 1 to 31 selects that day, clamped in shorter months. Explicit dates may recur later in the original month or year. Other frequencies require 0.

recurrence_weekdays.description: Weekly only: ISO weekdays (Monday=1, Sunday=7), stored in ascending order. Empty selects the original entry weekday. Weeks start Monday; every-N-week schedules remain anchored to the original entry week. Selected days later in the original week can recur. Other frequencies require an empty array.

recurrence_month.description: Yearly only: month 1 to 12, or 0 to use the original entry month. The year interval stays anchored to the entry year. Other frequencies require 0.

PersonalEntryInput.description: Native owner-protected expenses collection input. Recurrence metadata is managed by the server. The API-key automation endpoint accepts ExpenseInput only.

Overview.description: Complete-dataset monthly spending and personal income summary. total, previous, count, categories, activity and original_totals include personal expenses plus the user's positive allocated Circle expense shares when preferences.include_circle_in_budgets is enabled (the default). Circle categories use matching personal category names, falling back to Other. Personal income is reported separately; Circle income and repayments are excluded. Currency conversions are reference estimates rounded per personal expense or allocated share.

category.description: Personal category ID; empty for the unmatched Other report bucket.

category_name.description: Current display name for this report bucket.

previous_updated.description: Exact updated value from the personal record, checked inside the transaction.

CircleCategoryCopy.description: Owner/Admin replacement from the authenticated manager’s own personal settings. Copies names, colours, active status and order. Reuses matching Circle category IDs, removes unused unmatched categories, and archives unmatched categories used in history. Historical entries, monetary amounts and balances are preserved. The combined list is limited to 100 categories.

CircleApiExpenseInput.description: Creates an expense as the API key owner, who must be an active Circle member. paid_by and created_by are that membership ID. A percentage split assigns 10000 basis points (100%) and the entire amount to that same member, initially creating no shared debt. Payer, shares, split_mode, kind, recurrence and provenance fields are server-managed and rejected in requests. Edit allocations through the authenticated website. Optional Idempotency-Key header provides the same user-scoped, fixed 24-hour retry protection as the general endpoint.

amount.description: Integer minor units of the specified currency.

currency.description: Supported uppercase currency code. Omission uses the Circle currency. Amount is expressed in this currency minor units.

category.description: Active category NAME from the target Circle. The server resolves it to a stored relation ID. Omission selects Other or the first active Circle category.

occurred_at.description: ISO date with Z or an explicit offset. Omission uses server time.

CircleSettlementEdit.description: Replacement payer, recipient, currency and amount with the current version. Omitted notes and occurred_at preserve their saved values.

allocated_amount.description: The requesting account allocated share, in original currency minor units. Original amount remains the full Circle transaction amount.

budget_category.description: Matching personal category ID, or empty for an unmatched Other bucket.

membership_active.description: Whether the requesting account membership remains active. Inactive historical shares are readable but do not grant current Circle access.

budget_category_name.description: Current display label for the matched personal category or Other bucket.

input_mode.description: Subtotals require exactly one item per participant, assigned only to that member.

members.description: Circle membership IDs. Each line total is divided equally among these members with deterministic rounding.

discount.description: Discount in minor units, smaller than subtotal. Distributed proportionally before calculating charges.

service_rate_bp.description: 1000 = 10%. Applied to the discounted subtotal excluding included GST.

service_amount.description: Printed service charge in minor units, or null to calculate using the rate. Zero explicitly waives the charge.

gst_rate_bp.description: 900 = 9%. Added GST applies to discounted items plus service. Included GST is extracted from item prices; added service incurs additional GST.

gst_amount.description: Printed added GST amount, or null for automatic calculation. Must be null for included or no GST.

adjustment.description: Signed final adjustment for receipt rounding or other fees. Distributed proportionally; total must stay positive and shares non-negative.

CircleReceipt.description: Saved receipt calculation for expense entries with exact splits. The server recomputes amount and shares and rejects mismatches. At most 50 participants across all items. No floating-point money; all money is in currency minor units. Charges use receipt-level half-up rounding and deterministic largest-remainder allocation.

idempotency_expires_at.description: Fixed expiry based on the original server creation time; null when no key was supplied.
Fixed expiry based on the original server creation time; null when no key was supplied.

category.description: Active personal category relation ID. Omit to match the Circle category name against active personal categories, falling back to Other or the first active category.
Personal category relation ID, or empty for the overall monthly budget.

can_add.description: Allows new expenses and income, including API imports, personal-to-Circle moves and recurring generation. Defaults to true.

edit_scope.description: Own means created_by equals the member ID. Defaults to own.

delete_scope.description: Independent of Edit permission. Defaults to own.

move_scope.description: Independent Move to personal permission. none denies moves; payer requires paid_by to equal the acting membership ID; all allows any Circle expense or income to move in full into the acting user’s personal ledger. Does not depend on Add, Edit or Delete. New members default to payer. Owners and Admins have effective all access.

CirclePermissions.description: Effective transaction permissions for the current active member. The owner and Admins always have can_add=true and all scopes (including Move), regardless of stored member permissions.

can_add.description: Allows new expenses and income, including API imports, personal-to-Circle moves and recurring generation. Defaults to true.

edit_scope.description: Own means created_by equals the member ID. Defaults to own.

delete_scope.description: Independent of Edit permission. Defaults to own.

is_admin.description: Stored Admin permission, default false. Grants full transaction and Circle management access, including managing other members and Admin permissions. The owner cannot be removed or restricted; Circle deletion and ownership transfer remain owner-only. Admin includes full Move access to any Circle entry, even when another member paid.

move_scope.description: Independent Move to personal permission. none denies moves; payer requires paid_by to equal the acting membership ID; all allows any Circle expense or income to move in full into the acting user’s personal ledger. Does not depend on Add, Edit or Delete. New members default to payer. Owners and Admins have effective all access.
